item.text: {"analysis":"The trial completed successfully, but learned causal retrieval did not improve validation HR@10 over the supplied recurrent-memory reference: macro HR@10 was 0.5200 versus 0.5388, a decline of 0.0188. It remained above the supplied SASRec baseline of 0.5050 by 0.0150. Category HR@10 was 0.5800 for Movies_and_TV, 0.5800 for Industrial_and_Scientific, 0.4000 for Electronics, and 0.5200 for CDs_and_Vinyl. These results do not support replacing prefix-average memory with this attention implementation under the retained training setup; they do not establish why performance declined.","code_summary":"Trained one independent RecurrentMemory model per category, with hidden size 96, context length 64, and dropout 0.25. A GRU supplies queries to single-head causal attention over normalized item-embedding keys and values. Attention masks padding and future positions and safely zeros fully masked queries. Retrieved memory passes through a tanh projection and learned gate before residual addition and output normalization; tied item embeddings and item biases produce scores. Training retains 32 sampled negatives, masked sampled-softmax plus 0.2-weighted positive/negative BCE, AdamW, gradient clipping, and validation checkpoint selection. The predictor exports the exact architecture and loads one selected checkpoint per category, without ensembling."}
